_about: Category graph: meal-planning apps. Facts only, each taken from the app's own website, help docs or App Store listing on `lastVerified`. Never store review text or marketing prose. A null/'—' value means we could not verify it — leave it that way rather than guess. Consumed by scripts/generate-comparison-pages.js for `type: "app-roundup"` pages. MomRise facts come from the App Store listing plus the app code in lib/ (see `momriseCodeRefs`).

apps.name: MomRise
apps.platforms: iPhone only (iOS 14+). No Android or web app.
apps.groceryList: Yes — built automatically from the week's plan, sorted by aisle; can be sent to Instacart
apps.recipeImport: Recipe websites, TikTok links, photos/screenshots (e.g. Instagram posts, cookbook pages), pasted text; share from Pinterest
apps.kidFeatures: Profiles for each child, milestone tracker and age-based activity ideas. No picky-eater-specific meal tools.
apps.familySharing: Share a week, day, meal or recipe by link. No shared household login.
apps.whoFor: Moms of babies to early-school kids on iPhone who want the weekly meal plan, grocery list, family calendar, milestones and activity ideas in one app instead of several.
strengths: Meal planning, grocery list, family calendar, milestone tracking and activity ideas live in one app
Imports recipes from websites, TikTok links, screenshots or photos, and pasted text
Grocery list builds itself from the plan, groups items by aisle and can be sent to Instacart
Tracks several children in one place
drawbacks: iPhone only — no Android or web version
No free plan once the 7-day trial ends
New app with few App Store ratings so far (10 ratings when we checked)
Its built-in recipe collection is still growing, so expect to import your own favorites
No picky-eater or baby-led-weaning tools, and no shared household login
momriseCodeRefs: lib/components/parent_circle_widget.dart (partner is a display label, not a second login)

apps.name: Plan to Eat

price.summary: 14-day free trial, then $5.95/mo or $49/yr (website prices; in-app prices can differ)

apps.groceryList: Yes — generated from the meal plan, organized by store and aisle, with grocery delivery
apps.recipeImport: Any website, Instagram, TikTok and Pinterest via its Recipe Clipper; camera/photo import
apps.familySharing: Yes — one account can be shared by everyone in the household
apps.whoFor: Families who already have favorite recipes scattered across blogs and social media and want to plan the week from their own collection, on any device.
strengths: Built around your own recipes: clip from websites and social media, or import from a photo
Grocery list comes straight from the plan and is organized by store and aisle
Works on iPhone, Android and the web
One account can be shared across the household
drawbacks: No free plan after the trial
No kid-, baby- or picky-eater-specific features listed
It's a planner for your recipes, not a source of ready-made plans

sources.title: Plan to Eat — Meal Planner on the App Store

apps.name: Paprika Recipe Manager

price.freeTier: Yes — up to 50 recipes on one device, no time limit
price.summary: Free (up to 50 recipes); Premium is a subscription whose price varies by region and is shown in your app store

apps.groceryList: Yes — add a whole week to the list, organized by aisle or recipe (one list on the free version)
apps.recipeImport: Recipe websites (free); social media posts, copied text and cookbook-page scans (Premium)
apps.familySharing: Premium family accounts — family members share the owner's subscription
apps.whoFor: Recipe collectors who want a personal cookbook with meal planning and grocery lists across the widest range of devices, including Mac and Windows.
strengths: Free version with no time limit (up to 50 recipes)
Available on iPhone, iPad, Mac, Android and Windows
Website import on the free version; social, text and cookbook-page import with Premium
Premium family accounts share one subscription
drawbacks: Free version is limited to 50 recipes, one device and one grocery list
Premium price isn't published on its website (it varies by region)
No kid-, baby- or picky-eater-specific features listed

apps.name: Cozi Family Organizer

price.summary: Free; Cozi Gold $39/yr (ad-free); Cozi Max $79/yr (adds AI meal planner)

apps.groceryList: Yes — shared shopping lists; add a recipe's ingredients to a list
apps.recipeImport: Paste a recipe's web address, or share from Safari/Chrome
apps.kidFeatures: Shared family calendar and chore lists. No picky-eater tools.
apps.familySharing: Yes — the whole family shares one account, each signing in with their own email
apps.whoFor: Families whose main problem is coordination — one shared calendar, shopping list and to-do list for everyone — with meal planning as one part of it.
strengths: Free plan includes the meal planner, recipe box, shared grocery lists and shared calendar
Everyone in the family signs in to the same account
Works on iPhone, Android and the web
Planned meals show up on the family calendar
drawbacks: Ingredients go to the list recipe by recipe rather than from the whole week at once
The free plan isn't ad-free (ad-free is a Gold feature)
AI meal planning requires the $79/yr Max plan
No picky-eater or baby-feeding features

sources.title: Cozi Family Organizer on the App Store

apps.name: eMeals

price.summary: 14-day free trial; as low as $4.99/mo on a 12-month subscription, or $37.50 for 3 months

apps.groceryList: Yes — built automatically from the meals you pick; order through Walmart, Kroger, Amazon Fresh, Instacart and others
apps.recipeImport: Yes — add family recipes and recipes from the web
apps.kidFeatures: A Kid Friendly meal plan aimed at picky eaters
apps.whoFor: Busy parents who want someone else to write the weekly menu and want to send the grocery list straight to a delivery or pickup service.
strengths: Ready-made weekly meal plans, including a Kid Friendly plan
Shopping list is built for you and can go to several grocery delivery and pickup services
Also lets you add your own and web recipes
iPhone, Android and web
drawbacks: No free plan listed after the trial
Month-to-month price isn't published on its site
We couldn't confirm household sharing from its own pages

apps.name: Ollie
apps.platforms: Text messages on iPhone or Android — no app needed
apps.groceryList: Yes — written automatically from the plan, organized by aisle; can order through Amazon, Instacart or Walmart
apps.familySharing: Yes — add family members to a group text; one subscription covers the group
apps.whoFor: Parents who want to hand off meal planning entirely by texting an AI assistant, and don't need a recipe app.
strengths: Works over text messages — nothing to install
Plans meals around your family and writes the grocery list
Can order groceries through Amazon, Instacart or Walmart
Partners and helpers can join the same group text
drawbacks: Paid plans ($25 and $100 a month) cost more than every other app here
The free plan is capped by message count
We couldn't confirm recipe import or kid-specific features on its site

apps.name: Eat This Much

price.summary: Free (one day at a time); Premium $5/mo with an annual subscription

apps.groceryList: Premium — automatic grocery list with grocery delivery (Instacart, Amazon Fresh)
apps.recipeImport: Yes — share recipes from your browser; also accepts recipes shared from Meals Hub (Mealime's successor)
apps.kidFeatures: Meal settings for additional family members and family scaling. No picky-eater tools.
apps.whoFor: Parents who plan meals around calorie or nutrition targets and want the app to generate plans that hit them.
strengths: Free plan generates daily meal plans
Lets you set different nutrition targets for each day of the week
Premium plans a full week and builds the grocery list, with delivery integration
Imports recipes shared from your browser or from Meals Hub
drawbacks: Weekly planning and the automatic grocery list are Premium-only
Built around nutrition targets more than kids' tastes — no picky-eater features
We couldn't confirm household sharing from its own pages

sources.title: Eat This Much — Meal Planner on the App Store

apps.name: Feeding Littles

price.freeTier: Yes — 75+ recipes, meal planner, grocery list, 5 recipe imports

apps.platforms: iPhone, Android. No web or desktop version.
apps.groceryList: Yes — created automatically, sorted by aisle
apps.recipeImport: Instagram, TikTok, websites, PDFs and screenshots (5 on free, unlimited on Premium)
apps.kidFeatures: Baby-led-weaning-friendly recipes with serve-safely photos, picky-eating tips; created by a dietitian
apps.familySharing: Premium household of up to 6 people; works with Apple Family Sharing
apps.whoFor: Parents of babies and toddlers starting solids or baby-led weaning who want feeding-focused recipes alongside a family meal planner.
strengths: Built for feeding young kids: baby-led-weaning-friendly recipes with serve-safely photos and picky-eating tips
Usable free plan with a planner, recipes and an automatic grocery list
Imports from Instagram, TikTok, websites, PDFs and screenshots
Premium household for up to 6 people
drawbacks: Only 5 recipe imports on the free plan
Premium costs $9.99/mo — more than the other recipe apps here that publish a monthly price
No web or desktop version

sources.title: Feeding Littles: Meal Planner on the App Store

apps.name: Little Lunches

price.freeTier: Free to start (trial; length not stated)
price.trial: Free trial, no credit card required

apps.groceryList: Yes — created automatically; Instacart and Walmart delivery in the US
apps.kidFeatures: Weekly plans from baby to teen: baby-led weaning, age-appropriate foods from 6–24 months, toddler meals, lunchbox ideas, picky-eater feeding support
apps.familySharing: Yes — add a second parent or caregiver free
apps.whoFor: Parents of picky eaters and school-age kids who want ready-made kid-focused weekly plans and lunchbox ideas.
strengths: Weekly meal plans built for kids, from baby to teen
Picky-eater feeding support and lunchbox ideas
Automatic grocery lists with Instacart and Walmart delivery in the US
A second parent or caregiver can join free
drawbacks: We couldn't confirm importing recipes from websites
Trial length isn't stated on its site
App store prices may differ by location (per its pricing page)

sources.title: Little Lunches: Kids Meals on the App Store
